passages.text: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, speak to your people and tell them: ‘Suppose I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land choose a man from among them, appointing him as their watchman, and he sees the sword coming against that land and blows the ram’s horn to warn the people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me again.
He said these words to me.
He called me "Son of man."
He told me to speak to the people of Israel.
He told me to give them a message.
He said, "Suppose I bring a sword against a land."
The people of that land choose one man from among themselves.
They appoint this man to be their watchman.
The watchman sees the sword coming against the land.
He blows the ram’s horn.
He warns the people.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶל־ בְּנֵֽי־ עַמְּךָ֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶ֕רֶץ כִּֽי־ אָבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ חָ֑רֶב וְלָקְח֨וּ עַם־ הָאָ֜רֶץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ מִקְצֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ לָהֶ֖ם לְצֹפֶֽה׃ וְרָאָ֥ה אֶת־ הַחֶ֖רֶב בָּאָ֣ה עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְתָקַ֥ע בַּשּׁוֹפָ֖ר וְהִזְהִ֥יר אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then if anyone hears the sound of the horn but fails to heed the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
passages.sermon:
A person hears the sound of the horn.
This horn is a warning.
The person does not pay attention to the warning.
The sword comes to the land.
The sword takes that person away.
That person is responsible for his own death.
His blood is on his own head.
passages.original: וְשָׁמַ֨ע הַשֹּׁמֵ֜עַ אֶת־ ק֤וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר֙ וְלֹ֣א נִזְהָ֔ר וַתָּ֥בוֹא חֶ֖רֶב וַתִּקָּחֵ֑הוּ דָּמ֥וֹ בְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ יִֽהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Since he heard the sound of the horn but failed to heed the warning, his blood will be on his own head. If he had heeded the warning, he would have saved his life.
passages.sermon:
A man hears the sound of the horn.
He does not heed the warning.
He is responsible for his own death.
If he heeds the warning, he saves his life.
passages.original: אֵת֩ ק֨וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֤ר שָׁמַע֙ וְלֹ֣א נִזְהָ֔ר דָּמ֖וֹ בּ֣וֹ יִֽהְיֶ֑ה וְה֥וּא נִזְהָ֖ר נַפְשׁ֥וֹ מִלֵּֽט׃

passages.text: But if the watchman sees the sword coming and fails to blow the horn to warn the people, and the sword comes and takes away a life, then that one will be taken away in his iniquity, but I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.’
passages.sermon:
A watchman stands guard over the people.
He sees the sword coming.
He does not blow the horn.
He does not warn the people.
The people do not receive a warning.
The sword comes.
The sword takes a life from among the people.
That person dies because of his own iniquity.
I will hold the watchman accountable for that person's blood.
passages.original: וְ֠הַצֹּפֶה כִּֽי־ יִרְאֶ֨ה אֶת־ הַחֶ֜רֶב בָּאָ֗ה וְלֹֽא־ תָקַ֤ע בַּשּׁוֹפָר֙ וְהָעָ֣ם לֹֽא־ נִזְהָ֔ר וַתָּב֣וֹא חֶ֔רֶב וַתִּקַּ֥ח מֵהֶ֖ם נָ֑פֶשׁ ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ נִלְקָ֔ח וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיַּֽד־ הַצֹּפֶ֥ה אֶדְרֹֽשׁ׃ס

passages.text: As for you, O son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; so hear the word from My mouth and give them the warning from Me.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God appointed Ezekiel as a watchman.
Ezekiel was a watchman for the house of Israel.
God told Ezekiel to listen to His words.
God told Ezekiel to warn the people of Israel for Him.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֔ם צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֤ מִפִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר וְהִזְהַרְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: If I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you will surely die,’ but you do not speak out to dissuade him from his way, then that wicked man will die in his iniquity, yet I will hold you accountable for his blood.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the prophet Ezekiel.
God gives Ezekiel the role of a watchman for Israel.
God says to Ezekiel, “If I say to a wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’
and you do not warn that wicked man to turn from his way,
then that wicked man will die because of his own sin.
But I will hold you responsible for his blood.”
passages.original: בְּאָמְרִ֣י לָרָשָׁ֗ע רָשָׁע֙ מ֣וֹת תָּמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א דִבַּ֔רְתָּ לְהַזְהִ֥יר רָשָׁ֖ע מִדַּרְכּ֑וֹ ה֤וּא רָשָׁע֙ בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

passages.text: But if you warn the wicked man to turn from his way, and he does not turn from it, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life.
passages.sermon:
You are the son of man.
God made you a watchman for the house of Israel.
You warn the wicked man to turn from his way.
The wicked man does not turn from his way.
The wicked man will die in his iniquity.
You will save your own life.
passages.original: וְ֠אַתָּה כִּֽי־ הִזְהַ֨רְתָּ רָשָׁ֤ע מִדַּרְכּוֹ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְלֹא־ שָׁ֖ב מִדַּרְכּ֑וֹ ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ס

passages.text: Now as for you, son of man, tell the house of Israel that this is what they have said: ‘Our transgressions and our sins are heavy upon us, and we are wasting away because of them! How can we live?’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God told Ezekiel to speak to the house of Israel.
The house of Israel said, "Our transgressions are upon us."
They said, "Our sins are upon us."
They said, "Because of our sins, we are wasting away."
They asked, "How can we live?"
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹר֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֤ן אֲמַרְתֶּם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי־ פְשָׁעֵ֥ינוּ וְחַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּבָ֛ם אֲנַ֥חְנוּ נְמַקִּ֖ים וְאֵ֥יךְ נִֽחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Say to them: ‘As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked should turn from their ways and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ways! For why should you die, O house of Israel?’
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He is the living God.
He makes a solemn declaration.
He does not desire the death of wicked people.
He wants wicked people to turn from their evil ways.
He wants them to live.
He calls out to the people of Israel.
He says, "Turn from your evil ways."
He repeats, "Turn from your evil ways."
He asks, "Why should you die, house of Israel?"
passages.original: אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי־ אָ֣נִי׀ נְאֻ֣ם׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם־ אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם־ בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Therefore, son of man, say to your people: ‘The righteousness of the righteous man will not deliver him in the day of his transgression; neither will the wickedness of the wicked man cause him to stumble on the day he turns from his wickedness. Nor will the righteous man be able to survive by his righteousness on the day he sins.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God told Ezekiel to speak to the people of Israel.
God said, "The righteous person cannot rely on his past righteousness if he sins."
If a righteous person commits a sin, his righteousness will not save him on that day.
If a wicked person turns away from his wickedness, his past wickedness will not make him fall on that day.
If a righteous person sins, he cannot live by his righteousness on the day he sins.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹ֤ר אֶל־ בְּנֵֽי־ עַמְּךָ֙ צִדְקַ֣ת הַצַּדִּ֗יק לֹ֤א תַצִּילֶ֙נּוּ֙ בְּי֣וֹם פִּשְׁע֔וֹ וְרִשְׁעַ֤ת הָֽרָשָׁע֙ לֹֽא־ יִכָּ֣שֶׁל בָּ֔הּ בְּי֖וֹם שׁוּב֣וֹ מֵֽרִשְׁע֑וֹ וְצַדִּ֗יק לֹ֥א יוּכַ֛ל לִֽחְי֥וֹת בָּ֖הּ בְּי֥וֹם חֲטֹאתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If I tell the righteous man that he will surely live, but he then trusts in his righteousness and commits iniquity, then none of his righteous works will be remembered; he will die because of the iniquity he has committed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people through the prophet.
God describes a righteous man.
God says to the righteous man, “You will surely live.”
The righteous man trusts in his own righteousness.
The righteous man then commits sin.
God will not remember any of his righteous deeds.
God will judge him for the sin he has done.
He will die because of his sin.
passages.original: בְּאָמְרִ֤י לַצַּדִּיק֙ חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְהֽוּא־ בָטַ֥ח עַל־ צִדְקָת֖וֹ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֑וֶל כָּל־ צִדְקָתוֹ לֹ֣א תִזָּכַ֔רְנָה וּבְעַוְל֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה בּ֥וֹ יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: But if I tell the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right— if he restores a pledge, makes restitution for what he has stolen, and walks in the statutes of life without practicing iniquity—then he will surely live; he will not die.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the wicked man.
God says, “You will surely die.”
The wicked man turns away from his sin.
He does what is just and right.
He returns what he took as a pledge.
He pays back what he has stolen.
He follows the laws that lead to life.
He does not do evil anymore.
This man will surely live.
He will not die.
passages.original: וּבְאָמְרִ֥י לָֽרָשָׁ֖ע מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת וְשָׁב֙ מֵֽחַטָּאת֔וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃ חֲבֹ֨ל יָשִׁ֤יב רָשָׁע֙ גְּזֵלָ֣ה יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם בְּחֻקּ֤וֹת הַֽחַיִּים֙ הָלַ֔ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י עֲשׂ֣וֹת עָ֑וֶל חָי֥וֹ יִֽחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: None of the sins he has committed will be held against him. He has done what is just and right; he will surely live.
passages.sermon:
God judges each person fairly.
God does not hold past sins against a person who turns from evil.
If a person does what is just and right, God sees this.
If a person turns from sin and acts righteously, God forgives him.
God does not remember the sins he committed before.
This person will surely live.
passages.original: כָּל־ חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א לֹ֥א תִזָּכַ֖רְנָה ל֑וֹ מִשְׁפָּ֧ט וּצְדָקָ֛ה עָשָׂ֖ה חָי֥וֹ יִֽחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But it is their way that is not just.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel speak.
They say, "The way of the Lord is not just."
The people accuse God of being unfair.
But their own way is not just.
The people of Israel act unjustly.
passages.original: וְאָמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֔ לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י וְהֵ֖מָּה דַּרְכָּ֥ם לֹֽא־ יִתָּכֵֽן׃

passages.text: If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he will die for it.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man lives by doing what is right.
If this righteous man turns away from his righteousness, he stops doing what is right.
He then commits iniquity.
He does what is wrong.
He will die because of his iniquity.
passages.original: בְּשׁוּב־ צַדִּ֥יק מִצִּדְקָת֖וֹ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֑וֶל וּמֵ֖ת בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: But if a wicked man turns from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he will live because of this.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man does evil things.
He lives in wickedness.
If this wicked man turns away from his wickedness, he changes his ways.
He chooses to do what is just.
He chooses to do what is right.
Because he does what is just and right, he will live.
passages.original: וּבְשׁ֤וּב רָשָׁע֙ מֵֽרִשְׁעָת֔וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם ה֥וּא יִֽחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel said, “The way of the Lord is not just.”
The Lord answered the people of Israel.
The Lord said, “I will judge each person by his own ways.”
The Lord spoke this to the house of Israel.
passages.original: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י אִ֧ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֛יו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל פ

passages.text: In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and reported, “The city has been taken!”
passages.sermon:
We were in exile.
Twelve years had passed since our exile began.
It was the tenth month.
It was the fifth day of that month.
A fugitive came to me.
He came from Jerusalem.
He brought a report.
He said, “The city has been taken.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא־ אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Now the evening before the fugitive arrived, the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So my mouth was opened and I was no longer mute.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD gave me power.
This happened in the evening.
It was before the fugitive from Jerusalem arrived.
The LORD opened my mouth.
He did this before the man came to me in the morning.
My mouth was opened.
I was no longer mute.
passages.original: וְיַד־ יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בָּעֶ֗רֶב לִפְנֵי֙ בּ֣וֹא הַפָּלִ֔יט וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח אֶת־ פִּ֔י עַד־ בּ֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיִּפָּ֣תַח פִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱלַ֖מְתִּי עֽוֹד׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, those living in the ruins in the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land. But we are many; surely the land has been given to us as a possession.’
passages.sermon:
The word of the LORD came to me.
God spoke to me.
He called me “Son of man.”
He spoke about the people living in the ruins in the land of Israel.
These people are saying something.
They say, “Abraham was only one man.”
They say, “Abraham possessed the land.”
They say, “We are many people.”
They say, “Surely the land has been given to us as a possession.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם יֹ֠שְׁבֵי הֶחֳרָב֨וֹת הָאֵ֜לֶּה עַל־ אַדְמַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֹמְרִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶחָד֙ הָיָ֣ה אַבְרָהָ֔ם וַיִּירַ֖שׁ אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ רַבִּ֔ים לָ֛נוּ נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה׃ס

passages.text: Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You eat meat with the blood in it, lift up your eyes to your idols, and shed blood. Should you then possess the land?
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to the people of Israel who live in the ruins.
He says this to them.
You eat meat that still has blood in it.
You look up to your idols.
You shed blood.
Should you then possess the land?
passages.original: לָכֵן֩ אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה עַל־ הַדָּ֧ם׀ תֹּאכֵ֛לוּ וְעֵינֵכֶ֛ם תִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶל־ גִּלּוּלֵיכֶ֖ם וְדָ֣ם תִּשְׁפֹּ֑כוּ וְהָאָ֖רֶץ תִּירָֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: You have relied on your swords, you have committed detestable acts, and each of you has defiled his neighbor’s wife. Should you then possess the land?’
passages.sermon:
The Lord God speaks to the people living in the land of Israel.
You have trusted in your swords.
You have done what is detestable.
Each man has made his neighbor’s wife unclean.
Should you possess the land?
passages.original: עֲמַדְתֶּ֤ם עַֽל־ חַרְבְּכֶם֙ עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ן תּוֹעֵבָ֔ה וְאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־ אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ טִמֵּאתֶ֑ם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ תִּירָֽשׁוּ׃ס

passages.text: Tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘As surely as I live, those in the ruins will fall by the sword, those in the open field I will give to be devoured by wild animals, and those in the strongholds and caves will die by plague.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks with authority and power.
He says, "As surely as I live, I will act."
People live in the ruins.
They will fall by the sword.
People stay in the open fields.
I will give them to wild animals to be eaten.
People hide in strongholds and caves.
They will die by plague.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ תֹאמַ֨ר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם כֹּה־ אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֮ חַי־ אָנִי֒ אִם־ לֹ֞א אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֶּֽחֳרָבוֹת֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לַחַיָּ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יו לְאָכְל֑וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֛ר בַּמְּצָד֥וֹת וּבַמְּעָר֖וֹת בַּדֶּ֥בֶר יָמֽוּתוּ׃

passages.text: I will make the land a desolate waste, and the pride of her strength will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will become desolate, so that no one will pass through.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God says, "I will make the land empty and ruined."
I will destroy the land completely.
The land will have no life or activity.
The pride and power of the land will end.
The mountains of Israel will become deserted.
No one will travel through the mountains.
No one will pass by or live there.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֣ה וּמְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְנִשְׁבַּ֖ת גְּא֣וֹן עֻזָּ֑הּ וְשָֽׁמְמ֛וּ הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֵ֥ין עוֹבֵֽר׃

passages.text: Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have made the land a desolate waste because of all the abominations they have committed.’
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God will make the land empty and ruined.
God will do this because the people have done many evil things.
When God makes the land a waste, the people will know that He is the LORD.
passages.original: וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּתִתִּ֤י אֶת־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֣ה וּמְשַׁמָּ֔ה עַ֥ל כָּל־ תּוֹעֲבֹתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃ס

passages.text: As for you, son of man, your people are talking about you near the city walls and in the doorways of their houses. One speaks to another, each saying to his brother, ‘Come and hear the message that has come from the LORD!’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel, who is called "son of man."  
God told Ezekiel about the people of Israel.  
The people of Israel are Ezekiel’s own people.  
The people talk about Ezekiel.  
They talk near the city walls.  
They talk in the doorways of their houses.  
One person speaks to another person.  
Each man speaks to his brother.  
They say, "Come now."  
They say, "Let us hear the word."  
They say, "This word comes from the LORD."
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֔ם בְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ הַנִּדְבָּרִ֤ים בְּךָ֙ אֵ֣צֶל הַקִּיר֔וֹת וּבְפִתְחֵ֖י הַבָּתִּ֑ים וְדִבֶּר־ חַ֣ד אֶת־ אַחַ֗ד אִ֤ישׁ אֶת־ אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֹּֽאוּ־ נָ֣א וְשִׁמְע֔וּ מָ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר הַיּוֹצֵ֖א מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So My people come to you as usual, sit before you, and hear your words; but they do not put them into practice. Although they express love with their mouths, their hearts pursue dishonest gain.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel, the son of man.
God said, "Your people come to you as they always do.
They sit before you as my people.
They listen to your words.
But they do not do what you say.
They speak loving words with their mouths.
But their hearts follow their own selfish gain.
They do not obey my message.
They only care about their own profit."
passages.original: וְיָב֣וֹאוּ אֵ֠לֶיךָ כִּמְבוֹא־ עָ֞ם וְיֵשְׁב֤וּ לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ עַמִּ֔י וְשָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־ דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ וְאוֹתָ֖ם לֹ֣א יַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ כִּֽי־ עֲגָבִ֤ים בְּפִיהֶם֙ הֵ֣מָּה עֹשִׂ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֥י בִצְעָ֖ם לִבָּ֥ם הֹלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Indeed, you are to them like a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice, who skillfully plays an instrument. They hear your words but do not put them into practice.
passages.sermon:
You are a prophet among the people of Israel.
The people listen to you.
To them, you are like a singer of love songs.
You have a beautiful voice.
You play an instrument skillfully.
They hear your words.
They do not do what you say.
passages.original: וְהִנְּךָ֤ לָהֶם֙ כְּשִׁ֣יר עֲגָבִ֔ים יְפֵ֥ה ק֖וֹל וּמֵטִ֣ב נַגֵּ֑ן וְשָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־ דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ וְעֹשִׂ֥ים אֵינָ֖ם אוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: So when it comes to pass—and surely it will come—then they will know that a prophet has been among them.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people through Ezekiel.
God says something will happen.
This thing will surely come to pass.
When it happens, the people will know the truth.
They will know a prophet was among them.
passages.original: וּבְבֹאָ֑הּ הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֔ה וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י נָבִ֖יא הָיָ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽם׃ס
